what: Questset corpus gate, run on the files RECEIVED at the Miami server
licence: CC BY 4.0 - no clause 4, no clause 15, no cloud prohibition. CITATION.txt travels in the archive. BOXRR DUA machinery does NOT attach, and this corpus's freedom must not leak onto BOXRR-derived files.

transfer.route: rsync over SSH from AVALON ~/xfer/ (their HTTP server is SimpleHTTP/0.6, which does not implement Range, so curl -C - could not resume a partial download)
transfer.throughput_note: rsync ran at 117 kB/s against HTTP's 114 kB/s - the LINK was the constraint, not the server. Switching transport bought resumability, not speed; my initial reasoning that it would be faster was wrong.

per_file_verification.method: per-file sha256, not totals - the 191-byte BOXRR PROVENANCE delta is why

up_axis.not_an_averaging_artefact: per-file mean of means and frame-pooled mean BOTH give 0.934
up_axis.reading: cooking_simulator drags the pooled figure down; 0.866 is plausible physics for a game of looking down and reaching, not an error. Both figures clear the >0.9 criterion. BECAUSE ALL 123 FILES HASH-MATCH THEIRS, a differing statistic can only be a differing COMPUTATION, not differing data - the cross-machine gate logic applied to a corpus statistic. Worth one line from them on how theirs was computed.
up_axis.caveat_for_arms: the up-axis invariant is title-dependent here, so a per-title figure is the meaningful one and a pooled figure hides a 0.12 spread

rate_outliers.reading: two group-1 identities recorded at roughly double rate. Not a gate failure - the mean is 62.2 Hz and the criterion is a sane native rate - but it matters for resampling: a fixed target rate treats these four sessions differently from the other 116, and they are concentrated in two identities rather than spread.

corpus_facts_adopted_from_their_conversi.positions_are_ABSOLUTE: their earlier message said positions were relative to each session's initial position and that the static-cue audit would be misleading; they retracted it after checking a file. Head Y sits at real height (mean 1.454 m here), so the raw static-cue audit IS applicable and every raw Questset figure carries the usual placement caveat.
corpus_facts_adopted_from_their_conversi.identity_key: (group, order, user) as g<G>o<O>u<UU> - the source User column runs 0..14 inside EVERY (group,order) block, so keying on it alone silently merges four people into one and yields a 15-identity corpus with four sessions each
corpus_facts_adopted_from_their_conversi.one_sitting_per_user: no temporal separation, no cross-session cost payable, nothing sayable about persistence
corpus_facts_adopted_from_their_conversi.quaternion_order: scalar-first in source; |q| is permutation-invariant and CANNOT validate ordering, so the device-local-+Y-into-world invariant is the check that can
